headline: TREASURY DOUBLES LONG-DEBT BUYBACKS → GOLD LEAPS $100, GDX POSTS BEST SINGLE DAY IN FOUR YEARS
snippet: The U.S. Treasury announced on August 19 it will at least double its monthly liquidity-support buyback operations for long-dated government debt — starting September 9 at no less than $4 billion per month for securities in the 10-to-30-year sector — triggering a sharp drop in the 30-year yield from 5.33% to 5.19% and detonating a rally across precious metals and miners. Spot gold jumped over $100 to approximately $4,484 (up 3.46% on the session), silver climbed back above $65/oz, and the VanEck Gold Miners ETF (GDX) surged 8.8% to $96.88 — its largest single-day percentage gain in nearly four years. The move matters structurally: lower long-end yields compress the opportunity cost of holding gold, while producer leverage means a 3-4% move in bullion translates to an 8-13% move in miners. With the 30-year having been the key headwind since the 5.33% spike two days earlier, this announcement removes the near-term ceiling that had capped the August rally.

headline: FOMC MINUTES: THREE FED DISSENTERS CALLED FOR IMMEDIATE 25BP HIKE — "MANY" MEMBERS SAW FURTHER TIGHTENING NEEDED
snippet: Minutes from the July 29 FOMC meeting released August 19 confirmed that the 9-3 vote to hold rates at 3.50–3.75% masked a markedly more hawkish internal debate: Regional Fed Presidents Beth Hammack, Neel Kashkari, and Lorie Logan all voted for an immediate 25-basis-point hike, citing broad-based price pressures and concern that the AI investment boom and tariff-related supply shocks could entrench inflation. Critically, the minutes also showed that 'many' other participants — who voted with the majority to hold — assessed that further tightening would 'likely be necessary' if inflation did not decline, a formulation markets interpreted as warning against pricing in rate cuts. For gold and miners, the Treasury buyback announcement the same afternoon overwhelmed the hawkish minutes, sending yields back down and driving the precious metals surge. Jackson Hole on August 27–29 is now the binary event: Chair Warsh's first keynote as Chair will set the tone for September's meeting.

headline: HECLA AND COEUR SPIKE 13% AS SILVER MINERS OUTRUN GOLD MINERS IN TREASURY BUYBACK RALLY
snippet: While the GDX gained 8.8% on August 19, silver-focused producers Hecla Mining (NYSE: HL) and Coeur Mining (NYSE: CDE) each spiked 13% — outperforming diversified gold miners by a factor of roughly 1.5x as silver recovered above $65/oz after dipping below that level earlier in the week. The divergence illustrates a pattern that has recurred throughout this metals cycle: when yields fall quickly, silver's dual monetary-industrial demand profile amplifies its price move vs. gold, and silver-heavy miners carry additional operating leverage. For TSX-V silver explorers, this is the kind of session where producing peers put up the numbers — 13% in a day — that make venture boards revisit their pace of drilling. Silver is still up 53.9% year-over-year, and the gold-silver ratio that compressed to 67 is now tested again as both metals moved roughly in tandem on the buyback news.

headline: KARUS MINING (CSE: KARU) STARTS 7,500M SOUTH CARIBOO GOLD PROGRAM — ALL 3 COMPLETED HOLES HIT TARGET VEIN HORIZON
snippet: Karus Mining Inc. (CSE: KARU) reported August 19 that its 2026 drill program at the FG Gold Project in the South Cariboo Gold District of British Columbia is off to a strong structural start: 2,031 metres have been completed across six holes, and all three assay-ready holes successfully intersected the target structural horizon — providing early validation of the company's Sediment-Hosted Vein (SHV) geological model. The planned 7,500-metre core program is designed to extend and define two high-grade vein corridors identified in 2020–21, each running approximately 650 metres along strike and open to the northwest. Assays from the first holes are pending. For investors watching the South Cariboo gold district — which includes several active juniors drawn to the district's structural analogy with established vein-gold camps — structural confirmation in the first six holes is the kind of early result that keeps a small-cap exploration program on track and visible.

headline: GOLD UP 10% IN AUGUST — BEST MONTHLY GAIN SINCE JANUARY — CAN IT SURVIVE WARSH'S JACKSON HOLE TEST?
snippet: A Business Standard analysis published August 19 frames gold's 10% August gain — from near $4,000 to above $4,480 — as the metal's best monthly performance since January, driven by three sequential data misses (nonfarm payrolls down 23,000, soft CPI, weak retail sales) that cut September rate-hike odds from 50% to 31%. The piece poses the question the entire mining sector is watching: whether the rally can survive Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's debut Jackson Hole keynote on August 27–29. Warsh, who took office May 22, has signalled he will 'frame the big questions' at Wyoming — language markets took as a potential communication shift from the previous chair's forward guidance framework. A hawkish Warsh could test the $4,300 floor; a dovish framing extends the August breakout toward $4,600. Either way, the analysis notes that gold mine supply has grown less than 1% annually for a decade — the structural bull thesis is unaffected by a single speech.

headline: ENERGY FUELS (TSX:EFR) BETS $104M ON RARE EARTHS AT WHITE MESA — $725M DOE LOAN SECURED, FIRST HRE CIRCUITS ONLINE BY 2027
snippet: BNN Bloomberg's August 17 deep-dive on Energy Fuels (TSX: EFR / NYSE American: UUUU) profiles the company's aggressive pivot from uranium producer to rare earth superpower: construction began July 29 on a $104-million expansion of the White Mesa Mill in Utah to add commercial-scale heavy rare earth circuits, targeting 20 metric tonnes of terbium oxide and 120 metric tonnes of dysprosium oxide per year by end-2027, with samarium, europium, and gadolinium circuits following by end-2028. A conditional U.S. Office of Strategic Capital commitment for a 20-year loan of up to $725 million supports the expansion, which is sized around monazite feedstock from the Donald rare earth and mineral sands project in Australia — a joint venture with Astron Ltd. where Energy Fuels received Australian foreign investment approval in Q2 and expects the transaction to close before August 31. White Mesa would become the only plant in the Western Hemisphere capable of producing all four magnetic heavy rare earth oxides at commercial scale, positioning Energy Fuels between two critical segments — uranium and rare earths — that both benefit from current U.S. domestic supply chain policy.

headline: GLENCORE, ANGLO, RIO TINTO BOSSES: TOUGHER REGULATORY SCRUTINY WON'T STOP MINING M&A — COPPER ASSETS STILL IN PLAY
snippet: Senior executives from Glencore, Anglo American, and Rio Tinto stated at a Mining Weekly-reported industry forum on August 19 that rising regulatory scrutiny of large mining mergers — driven by governments' growing focus on critical mineral security and antitrust review of supply concentration — is increasing the complexity of deals but is not making major M&A unworkable. The executives cited national interest notifications, foreign investment review triggers, and critical mineral export control policies as factors that add 6–18 months to transaction timelines but rarely kill deals outright for well-structured transactions. With the Anglo American–Teck Resources merger progressing, the USA Rare Earth–Serra Verde deal pending shareholder approval August 28, and ongoing speculation around copper consolidation given Glencore's persistent interest in the sector, the message from majors is that the appetite for transformative copper-focused M&A remains high despite the scrutiny environment.

headline: GOLD SMELLS A RAT: TREASURY BUYBACKS LOOK LIKE BACKDOOR YIELD CURVE CONTROL — NOT A FREE-MARKET MOVE
snippet: The Daily Reckoning's August 19 contrarian take argues that the Treasury Department's announcement to double long-dated debt buybacks — framed officially as 'liquidity support' — is structurally indistinguishable from yield curve control: the government is effectively bidding up its own long-dated debt to suppress borrowing costs it cannot otherwise manage given $1.17 trillion in year-to-date interest expense. The piece notes that gold's $100 surge on the announcement — before any Fed action, before any rate change — is the market assigning a monetary debasement premium in real time. The argument: when a government with a $1.8 trillion year-to-date fiscal deficit begins systematically buying its own long-term bonds, gold holders are right to treat this as a structural change in the debt-management regime, not a routine liquidity operation. This is exactly the kind of institutional credibility erosion that drives sustained gold demand across the 12-to-36-month horizon, regardless of what any one FOMC meeting decides.

headline: PAN AMERICAN, ALAMOS, IAMGOLD, ENDEAVOUR: TOP GOLD PRODUCERS TO WATCH AS SECTOR OUTPERFORMS IN AUGUST 2026
snippet: Kalkine's August 2026 roundup of top gold producer stocks highlights four mid-to-large-cap names generating strong cash flow at current gold prices: Pan American Silver (TSX: PAAS), which benefits from both gold and silver exposure across its Americas portfolio; Alamos Gold (TSX: AGI), whose Island Gold expansion is tracking to become one of Canada's lowest-cost underground mines; IAMGOLD (TSX: IMG), rebuilding its balance sheet after the Côté Gold mine ramp-up; and Endeavour Mining (TSX: EDV), the West Africa operator generating strong margins at Sabodala-Massawa and Lafiguè. With gold now above $4,480 and GDX up 8.8% on August 19, the larger producers are finally closing the valuation gap to the metal itself — a gap that Hamilton Analytics noted had pushed the GDX P/E to 16.5x, the lowest in 41 quarters. For retail investors entering the sector, these four names represent the established-producer layer above the more speculative junior exploration tier.
